overall_why: C over B: both open on almost nothing and one Return gets me in. C's page is a date, 'Pick up where you stopped on Tuesday' and a line to write on (concept-c/shots/s1-cold-dark, concept-c/window/s1-cold-light). B's is three lines and '↩ carry on' (concept-b/shots/s1-cold-dark). What tipped it is what happens once I'm in. C always tells me where talk goes ('Or write on the page' under the task, 'Esc: back to the task'). C also keeps the plan in the margin, and the plan changes in place with 'moved up', 'moved down' and 'Moved from Sun 22 Nov' (concept-c/window/s3-after-dark, concept-c/live/s3-after-light). C's tangent is labelled as unmarked and it comes straight back to the open task (concept-c/live/s4-return-dark). B hides the plan behind ⌘P. B says 'Marked right, on your own.' twice and 'The plan changed' twice (concept-b/window/s2-answer-dark, concept-b/window/s3-after-light). In the live run, the B screen after the plan change shows my message and a footer line but not the tutor's reply (concept-b/live/s3-after-dark). B over A: for me, starting is the whole problem, and B is the build I'd least want to close. It never asks me anything: 'Sampling distributions ... ↩ start' (concept-b/window/s1-cold-dark). A is the better-made app and has the best plan view (concept-a/live/s3-after-dark). But it puts a programmer's editor around my lesson: tabs, a status bar, a 14-command list, and settings as a code file (concept-a/shots/settings-dark). Its first-run page has a paragraph, three ticks and three buttons (concept-a/window/s1-cold-first-light). A new course opens on a question, 'What do you want to work on?' (concept-a/window/s1-cold-dark). The plan pane is full of amber bars and struck-through dates. A wins more of the seven measures than B, but it loses calm and easy to start, and those two decide whether I open it at all.

by_measure_why.mine: C feels like my notebook: today's date, my own lines, earlier days below, and the record's marks small in the margin ('right / unaided', 'not right', 'no mark') (concept-c/shots/s2-answer-dark, concept-c/shots/s5-week-light). A reopens with my half-written working under the task, which really is mine (concept-a/shots/s1-cold-light). But the tabs, the status bar and the code-file settings make it feel like someone else's tool that I'd have to learn (concept-a/shots/settings-dark). B has the least app on screen, but marks come out in accent colour and twice ('Marked right, on your own.') (concept-b/shots/s2-answer-light). After a week the earlier conversation is gone from the page (concept-b/window/s5-week-next-dark), so it feels least like a record of my own work. A beat B on that half-written working.
by_measure_why.calm: B's cold screen is a course name, a title, where I stopped, and one line (concept-b/shots/s1-cold-dark, concept-b/shots/s5-week-light). Nothing else to look at. C is nearly as quiet (concept-c/shots/s1-cold-light), but in a lesson it adds a margin agenda and five little words under every task ('Hint I'm lost I don't know Photo Symbols') (concept-c/window/s2-start-dark). A always has tabs and a status bar. Its plan change opens a second pane of dates, amber bars and strikethroughs (concept-a/shots/s3-after-dark), and its first-run page is a small wall (concept-a/window/s1-cold-first-dark).
by_measure_why.easy_to_start: B: one Return and I'm in, and the line even invites 'or say what you would rather do'. Nothing is decided for me in a way that feels like a test, and after a week it says 'First: reading Vmax from the y-intercept, from Thu 5 Nov' with no count (concept-b/shots/s5-week-dark, concept-b/window/s1-cold-light). C: one Return, worded as my own work, 'Pick up where you stopped on Thursday 5 November', and a new course just says 'Start on Midterm 2' (concept-c/window/s5-week-dark, concept-c/live/c1-cold-light). Its 'Return' chip is small and grey, though. A: the returning screen has the clearest button of all, a big 'Continue Return' (concept-a/shots/s1-cold-dark). But a new course asks 'What do you want to work on?' with a list (concept-a/window/s1-cold-dark), and the first-run page asks me to read a paragraph and pick from three buttons (concept-a/window/s1-cold-first-light). That's deciding before starting.
by_measure_why.flexible: C: a labelled line under the task is always there for talk. The plan stays in view and changes in place with 'moved up / moved down'. The tangent says nothing is marked, and 'back to the task' returns to it (concept-c/live/s3-after-dark, concept-c/live/s4-offplan-light, concept-c/live/s4-return-dark). In my turn, typing 'change the plan' into the answer box was still treated as talk. A: the plan opens beside the lesson with every moved block marked, the open task stays pinned at the top, and Tab gets me back (concept-a/live/s3-after-light, concept-a/live/s4-offplan-dark). But the talk line is a bare unlabelled rule (concept-a/window/s4-offplan-dark). When I typed the plan change into the answer box, it was shown as a handed-in answer with 'No mark, not taken as the answer' under it. B: it works, and the open task waits dimmed at the foot (concept-b/window/s4-offplan-dark). But the plan is only behind ⌘P, and the live plan-change screen doesn't show the tutor's reply (concept-b/live/s3-after-light).
by_measure_why.craft: A is the tidiest and most consistent: the same tabs, headings, maths and blue ink for my words in both schemes and at the narrow size (concept-a/shots/narrow-lesson-light, concept-a/window/s2-answer-dark). C is clean and consistent too (concept-c/shots/narrow-lesson-dark). But the tool row is fussy, and the same task block gets reprinted above every message I send while it is open (concept-c/window/s4-offplan-dark, my turn). B has visible slips. The course name above the lesson title is clipped and faded (concept-b/window/s2-start-light). Lines are duplicated (concept-b/window/s2-answer-dark). In the narrow dark view, text slides under the input (concept-b/shots/narrow-lesson-dark).
by_measure_why.clarity: C puts the next action right under the box ('Esc: write on the page', 'Esc: back to the task', '⌘. stops the reply'). A green 'The plan changed.' line says what just happened, and the margin says how the record marked each answer, including 'no mark' (concept-c/shots/s3-after-light, concept-c/window/s3-before-dark). One slip: in the demo, 'back to the task' returned to a question I had already answered (concept-c/shots/s4-return-dark). A is explicit ('Continue Return', 'Not right yet', 'No mark, not taken as the answer', 'Plan changed at 18:15'), but most hints sit in a status bar at the bottom edge, far from where I'm looking. The talk line has no label (concept-a/window/s3-after-dark). B uses '›', '↑ answer' and 'esc talk instead' in tiny lowercase, and '⌘K start without them' left me guessing (concept-b/shots/s5-week-dark, concept-b/window/s4-offplan-light).
by_measure_why.performance: In practice the three are the same: input median 17 ms, p95 19 ms, max 20 ms for all three in window/perf.json. Startup (first/main/week): A 809/628/575 ms, B 850/620/567, C 805/615/644. In my own turns the startup was A 721 ms, B 727 ms and C 822 ms, with input A 17/19/20, B 17/18/19 and C 17/19/20. A has the lowest total startup and the best figure in my turn. B's slowest first open (850 ms) puts it behind A. C's 644 ms week startup and 822 ms in my turn put it last. All of these are well under a second, so I would not notice any difference.

concept-a: The editor costume: tabs, a status bar, a 14-command ⌘K list, and settings as a code file to edit (concept-a/shots/settings-dark, concept-a/shots/commands-dark). Too much to learn when all I want is to start.

The place to talk is a bare unlabelled line, and the hints live in the bottom status bar (concept-a/window/s4-offplan-dark). When I typed 'change the plan' into the answer box, it showed as a handed-in answer with 'No mark, not taken as the answer' under it, and for a second I thought I'd submitted it.

The first-run page (paragraph, three ticks, three buttons) and the new-lesson question 'What do you want to work on?' (concept-a/window/s1-cold-first-light, concept-a/window/s1-cold-dark). The plan pane's amber bars and struck-through dates read like corrections on my schedule (concept-a/live/s3-after-dark).
concept-b: Everything gets said twice: 'Marked right, on your own.' under my answer and again under the input, and 'The plan changed' as a card and again as a footer (concept-b/window/s2-answer-dark, concept-b/window/s3-after-light). It feels announced at me.
The plan is hidden behind ⌘P. In the live run, the screen after the plan change has no visible reply from the tutor, just a footer line (concept-b/live/s3-after-dark).

Cryptic tiny hints ('›', '↑ answer', 'esc talk instead', '⌘K start without them'). The course name at the top of a lesson is clipped and faded, and after a week away my earlier conversation isn't on the page (concept-b/window/s2-start-light, concept-b/window/s5-week-next-dark).
concept-c: Five little words under every task ('Hint I'm lost I don't know Photo Symbols'): useful when stuck, clutter the rest of the time (concept-c/window/s2-start-dark).

While a task is open, it gets reprinted above every message I send, so the same question piled up three times in my turn (also concept-c/window/s4-offplan-dark). In the demo, 'back to the task' returned to a question I had already answered (concept-c/shots/s4-return-dark).
The 'Return' chip on the cold page is small and grey, so it's easy to miss that it's the button. The big date heading on top of every page is a bit formal (concept-c/window/s1-cold-light).

window_turns: Same steps in each window, in the order C, A, B: open cold, press Return, type 'b = 5', then 'b = -5', then 'I skipped three days and the midterm moved, change the plan' into whichever box had focus, then 'By the way, what is a p-value?', then 'OK, back to the task.', then measure typing. The window's own start posed a standard-error question, so 'b = 5' was marked wrong and 'b = -5' got no mark. All three were honest about it. C showed 'not right' then 'no mark' in the margin. A showed '✕ Not right yet' then '– No mark, not taken as the answer'. B showed 'Not right yet.' then nothing. C: the cold page was a date, 'Start on Midterm 2' and a line to write on. The plan change typed in the answer box was treated as talk. The margin agenda moved the exam to Sun 29 Nov with 'moved up / moved down' plus a green 'The plan changed.' line. The tangent was unmarked and the return went straight back to the task. But the task block was reprinted above each of my messages. Startup 822 ms, input 17/19/20 ms. A: the cold page asked 'What do you want to work on?' with Sampling distributions preselected, and Return started it. The plan change typed in the answer box showed as an answer with 'No mark, not taken as the answer', and the plan opened in a second pane with amber bars and struck-through dates. The talk line after that was a bare rule, and the hints were in the status bar. The return worked. Startup 721 ms, input 17/19/20 ms. B: the cold page was three lines and '↩ start', and Return started it. The plan change got an inline 'The plan changed' card, repeated in a footer, and the whole plan only behind ⌘P. The tangent left the task dimmed at the foot, and the return brought it back. The course name above the lesson title was clipped. Startup 727 ms, input 17/18/19 ms.
